problemStatement.formal: Let d_k(p) be the density of integers whose k-th smallest prime factor is p. For fixed k ≥ 1, is d_k(p) unimodal in p?
problemStatement.plain: Is the density of integers whose k-th smallest prime factor equals p a unimodal function of p?
whyMatters: Connects prime factorization structure to density functions
Resolved for small k by Cambie (2025): yes for k ≤ 3, no for 4 ≤ k ≤ 20
Illustrates discrepancy between typical and modal prime factor sizes

proven: Cambie (2025): d_k(p) NOT unimodal for 4 ≤ k ≤ 20
Erdős: p_k(n) ≈ e^{e^k} for almost all n
Erdős: max of d_k at p ≈ e^{(1+o(1))k}
open: Exact characterization of which k give unimodality
